docs.title: Statistics this project actually runs
docs.text:
Graph theory stops when \(s_i\) and AI exist. The rest is ordinary biomedical statistics. Mixing the two layers — treating a GLM as if it were a new network invariant — is how papers become unreproducible.

This page is the statistical stack as implemented, with the literature it sits in, and the disagreements that look like “maths changes” but are not.

docs.title: Per-subject features (the input to statistics)
docs.text:
From Node strength and Asymmetry:

  • Node strength, intrahemispheric, interhemispheric
  • Side AI, optional SOZ-aligned AI, log-ratio
  • Optional volume and volume AI
  • Optional global strength \(\frac12\sum_i s_i\) as a covariate

These are features. They are not p-values.

docs.title: ROC for a single biomarker
docs.text:
Given a scalar (hippocampal AI, volume AI) and a binary label (left-HS vs control):

  • Plot TPR vs FPR as the threshold moves; AUC is \(P(\text{score}_{\mathrm{pos}}>\text{score}_{\mathrm{neg}})\) for a continuous score (Hanley & McNeil 1982).
  • Correlated AUCs (same patients, two biomarkers): DeLong, DeLong & Clarke-Pearson 19881.
  • An operating point \(\Rightarrow\) sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV. PPV/NPV need prevalence; AUC does not.

Threshold rules are not unique:

Rule What it optimises Closest to \((0,1)\) in ROC space Euclidean geometry on the unit square Youden \(J=\mathrm{sens}+\mathrm{spec}-1\) Youden 19502 MATLAB perfcurve optrocpt Toolbox default — not always either of the above A clinically chosen TPR e.g. “we will not miss more than 10% of HS”

AUC can match to \(10^{-15}\) while sensitivity/specificity differ. If a MATLAB table used pos_label=0 for patients, sklearn pos_label=1 maps \(\mathrm{AUC}\mapsto 1-\mathrm{AUC}\). That is a codebook issue. Do not change strengths_und to chase it. See Asymmetry.

docs.title: Normative models (Piper design)
docs.text:
Piper et al. 2026 residualise each nucleus’s strength in controls with a general linear model of age, sex, motion, and global brain strength, then z-score patients against the control residual SD3. Volumes use age, sex, and intracranial volume.

This package implements that design with OLS (numpy.linalg.lstsq in nodestrength.normative):

\[ y = X\beta + \varepsilon, \qquad \hat\beta = (X^\top X)^{+} X^\top y, \qquad z = \frac{y-X\hat\beta}{\hat\sigma} \]

where \(X\) has an intercept, continuous covariates as-is, and categorical covariates one-hot with drop_first=True. Residual SD uses \(\mathrm{ddof}=p\). Fits are per (nucleus, side) so right-sided patients are z-scored against right-sided control residuals.

The broader normative modelling literature (Marquand et al. 2016, 20194; GAMLSS) writes the same idea as a conditional distribution of the response given covariates \(x\):

\[ y \mid x \sim f\bigl(\hat{\mu}(x),\; \hat{\sigma}(x),\; \ldots\bigr) \]

Here \(\hat{\mu}(x)\) is the estimated mean (or location) at age/sex/motion/global strength, \(\hat{\sigma}(x)\) is an optional scale function, and \(f\) is a named family (Gaussian for OLS; more flexible in GAMLSS). A patient z-score is then \((y-\hat{\mu}(x))/\hat{\sigma}(x)\). Piper’s GLM is the Gaussian, homoscedastic case: \(\hat{\sigma}\) does not depend on \(x\), and \(\hat{\mu}(x)=x^\top\hat\beta\).

A penalised spline GAM (pygam, mgcv) is a different estimator for \(\mu(x)\). If you need splines, fit them outside this CLI and say so. Bayesian linear models in large biobanks are another option in that same family.

nodestrength fit-normative --controls controls.csv --out model.pkl pickles the OLS fits. dkt-ai-cohort --participants can fit from the control rows (--control-group) or load --normative-model.

docs.title: Mixed-design GLM / MANOVA
docs.text:
Piper reports Pillai’s trace and partial η² for within-subject factors (nucleus, side) and between-subject factors (group, SOZ, outcome) — the SPSS GLM multivariate repeated-measures convention.

nodestrength.stats implements the wide multivariate form (Rencher, Methods of Multivariate Analysis; Bakeman 2005 for multivariate partial η² \(= V/s\)):

  • Outcome matrix \(Y\) has one column per within-cell (e.g. 4 nuclei × 2 sides).
  • Between-subject design \(X\).
  • Hypothesis \(LB M = 0\) with \(L\) picking between-effects and \(M\) an orthonormal within-contrast.
  • Hypothesis and error SSP matrices \(H\), \(S\); Pillai \(V=\mathrm{tr}(H(H+S)^{-1})\); \(F\) approximation; partial η².

These will not bit-match SAS PROC GLM in the 7th decimal. Reproduce the design, not the binary of a floating-point trace.

Permutation analogue: PALM (Winkler et al. 2014)5; Freedman–Lane. Use those if exchangeability is clearer than Pillai’s \(F\).

CLI:

nodestrength analyze --cohort long.csv \
    --within nucleus side --between group \
    --value strength --out glm.csv

docs.title: Multiple comparisons
docs.text:
• Few planned hippocampal tests (left-HS vs control on hippocampal AI at one scale, one weight): report the raw p, AUC, and effect size. Bonferroni on four planned tests is fine.
  • Whole-atlas strength maps (84 or 462 nodes): FDR (Benjamini–Hochberg 1995) or a permutation max-statistic. Do not treat neighbouring parcels as independent.
  • Do not treat 4 scales × 5 weights × 2 reconstructions as independent discoveries of the same hippocampus. Pre-register the primary (\(W\), scale) pair; the rest are sensitivity analyses.
  • Edgewise maps: NBS, not Bonferroni on \(n(n-1)/2\) edges.

Button et al. (2013) on power in neuroscience: a Cohen’s \(d\) of 0.3 on \(n=20\) vs \(n=20\) is mostly noise. 288 subjects helps; 50 uncorrected BCT metrics undoes that help.

docs.title: What is not a maths change
docs.text:
Reimplementing strengths_und and AI in Python, with the same LUT order and the same \(W\), should match MATLAB/BCT to \(\sim 10^{-15}\). If it does, nobody changed the formula. Remaining disagreements are:

  1. Different \(W\) (det vs prob, SIFT, Count vs FA)
  2. Different LUT order (GraphML vs FreeSurfer LUT)
  3. Different intrahemispheric mask
  4. Different ROC operating point / pos_label
  5. GAM vs OLS
  6. Missing subjects (NaN isControl on rows without a connectome)
  7. SPSS vs NumPy Pillai

Those are data and estimator issues. The IDEAS replication trail in this project’s research notes is exactly that list: bitwise-identical AI when \(W\) and LUT match; different AUC when true deterministic Count replaces a copied probabilistic matrix; different sens/spec when optrocpt is not closest-to-(0,1).

  1. DeLong ER, DeLong DM, Clarke-Pearson DL. Comparing the areas under two or more correlated ROC curves. Biometrics. 1988;44:837–845. ↩

  2. Youden WJ. Index for rating diagnostic tests. Cancer. 1950;3:32–35. ↩

  3. Piper RJ et al. Epilepsia. 2026;67:1901–1915. ↩

  4. Marquand AF et al. Understanding heterogeneity in clinical cohorts using normative models. Biol Psychiatry. 2016;80:552–561. ↩

  5. Winkler AM et al. NeuroImage. 2014;92:381–397. ↩

docs.title: Node strength
docs.text:
Node strength is the weighted analogue of degree: the sum of edge weights incident on a node (Barrat et al. 20041; Opsahl, Agneessens & Skvoretz 20102; Rubinov & Sporns 20103).

\[ s_i = \sum_{j \in V,\, j \neq i} w_{ij} \]

For an undirected connectome this package first replaces \(W\) with \((W+W^\top)/2\) and sets \(w_{ii}=0\). That is BCT strengths_und, and it is what nodestrength compute-strength and dkt-ai-cohort print.

If bctpy is installed, the canonical BCT implementation is used; otherwise an equivalent NumPy row-sum after symmetrisation. With the same \(W\), the two match to numerical precision.

docs.title: Degree versus strength versus “hub”
docs.text:
Quantity On binary \(A\) On weighted \(W\) How many neighbours? Degree \(k_i\) — (or count of \(w_{ij}>0\)) How much connection mass? Same as degree Strength \(s_i\) How central in paths / modules? Betweenness, participation, … Same family on a distance transform

A node can have low degree and high strength (few but very heavy edges) or the reverse. Opsahl et al. (2010) interpolate with \(k_i (s_i/k_i)^\alpha\). We use \(\alpha=1\): pure strength.

Hub in the network-neuroscience sense (Sporns, Honey & Kötter 2007; van den Heuvel & Sporns 20134) is not strength. Provincial vs connector hubs need a community partition. Rich-club membership needs \(\phi(k)\) versus a null. Strength is necessary but not sufficient.

docs.title: What it means biologically (structural MRI)
docs.text:
If \(w_{ij}\) is a SIFT2-weighted streamline count, \(s_i\) is a reconstruction of how much white-matter connection mass parcel \(i\) participates in. It is not:

  • the number of synapses or axons (Jones, Knösche & Turner 20135)
  • a guarantee of a true anatomical projection (Maier-Hein 20176; Thomas 2014)
  • independent of parcel volume, reconstruction, or requested streamline count

If \(w_{ij}\) is mean FA, \(s_i\) mixes how many reconstructed connections with how anisotropic those connections are — a microstructure-weighted load, a different construct. If \(w_{ij}\) is mean length, \(s_i\) is a millimetre-sum, not wiring mass.

Always name the edge. See Connectomics.

docs.title: Intrahemispheric and interhemispheric strength
docs.text:
Let \(H(i)\) be the hemisphere of node \(i\).

Intrahemispheric strength (IDEAS hippocampus default):

\[ s_i^{\mathrm{intra}} = \sum_{j: H(j)=H(i),\, j\neq i} w_{ij} \]

Interhemispheric strength:

\[ s_i^{\mathrm{inter}} = \sum_{j: H(j)\neq H(i)} w_{ij} \]

dkt-ai-cohort writes all three (strength, strength_intra, strength_inter) so laterality of a deep nucleus is not dominated by the corpus callosum. Piper et al. 2026’s global brain strength covariate is the unmasked whole-brain sum (used in the normative GLM), not the intra mask.

Whole-brain undirected total weight is \(\frac{1}{2}\sum_i s_i\) (each edge counted twice in the \(s_i\) sum).

docs.title: Normalisation and confounds
docs.text:
Raw \(s_i\) scales with:

  • number of streamlines requested (tckgen -select)
  • SIFT2 on/off
  • det vs prob
  • brain size and parcel volume (bigger parcels collect more streamlines — a well-known bias)
  • head motion, in some pipelines
Approach Idea Caveat CountScaled divide edges or strength by volume and/or length Which divisor? Inconsistent across labs Strength fraction \(s_i / \sum_k s_k\) Loses a global hypo-connectivity effect Covariate global strength Piper 2026 GLM/OLS Preferred when you care about residual regional effects Consistency thresholding keep edges present in a fraction of subjects Changes topology; a different paper MST density-free backbone Stam 2014; discards cycles

There is no universally correct normalisation. Report the one you used. This CLI exposes raw strength (and intra/inter) and, with --participants, OLS residuals against controls.

docs.title: Strength versus volume
docs.text:
Grey-matter volume of the same parcel is a different measurement (FreeSurfer aseg/aparc or voxel count on dk_nodes.mif). In hippocampal sclerosis, volume loss is the textbook MRI finding. Connectivity strength asks whether remaining tissue is also under-wired. The two can disagree:

  • small but well-connected remnant
  • normal-sized but disconnected parcel (less common, but possible with reconstruction failure)

--with-volume-ai writes both, plus compare/strength_vs_volume_ai.csv. Volume AI uses the same laterality formula as strength AI (Asymmetry).

docs.title: Directed graphs
docs.text:
If you ever keep \(W\) asymmetric:

\[ s_i^{\mathrm{out}}=\sum_j w_{ij},\qquad s_i^{\mathrm{in}}=\sum_j w_{ji} \]

BCT strengths_dir. Macroscale tractography polarity is not axon polarity; this package treats graphs as undirected unless you have a genuine directed measurement (tracers, some functional models).

docs.title: Implementation notes
docs.text:
• NaNs in \(W\) become 0 (missing edge, not infinite weight).
  • Non-square matrices are rejected.
  • Isolated nodes get \(s_i=0\); they remain in the table so AI can be undefined (L+R=0) rather than silently dropped.
  • Isolated from a bad LUT (wrong row order) looks like “low strength.” Always check LUT provenance before interpreting a clinical effect.

docs.text:
